PROMISE: Establish 1.5 lakh health and wellness centres under Ayushman Bharat.
STATUS AND COMMENTS: - 1.5 lakh Health and Wellness Centres operational under Ayushman Bharat as of 2023. | - Achieved before the end of December 2022, as per Economic Survey 2022-23.

PROMISE: Start setting up 75 new Medical Colleges/Post Graduate Medical Colleges.
STATUS AND COMMENTS: - Scheme implemented in three phases, with Phase-III (started in 2019) aimed at 75 new medical colleges in various aspirational districts. | - So far, 157 new medical colleges sanctioned under this scheme since its inception. | - Phase-I: 50 out of 58 medical colleges operational. | - Phase-II: 8 colleges operational. | - Phase-III: 14 out of 75 colleges functional. | - Goal for 2023-24 session to commence undergraduate courses, but challenging due to slow pace of progress.

PROMISE: Enhance healthcare through digital means, including telemedicine.
STATUS AND COMMENTS: - Market Value: Grew to $1.10 billion in 2022 and expected to reach $5.15 billion by 2030, indicating significant growth accelerated by the COVID-19 pandemic. | - National Health Digital Mission: Focuses on unique health identification and electronic health records. | - Achievements: Telemedicine has improved patient-provider satisfaction and cost-effectiveness, especially during the pandemic. | - Government Initiatives: Supported initiatives like the National Rural Telemedicine Network. | - Challenges: Persist especially in rural areas, including digital literacy, connectivity, awareness, and healthcare infrastructure. The gap between urban and rural healthcare services remains a concern.

- Lack of Robust Foster Care System and Family-Based Alternatives: India has a large number of orphaned and vulnerable children (OVC), with CCIs often being the only option due to the lack of strong foster care or other family-based care alternatives. | - Limitations of CCIs: Despite the Juvenile Justice Act allowing for non-institutional alternatives, CCIs remain a default option, which poses various issues. | - Role of Care in CCIs: The care within CCIs can provide primary protective value, depending on the resources available, such as education and positive peer groups. | - Quality of Resources and Guidance in CCIs: The quality of education, extracurricular opportunities, and guidance in CCIs greatly influences the initial adjustment and long-term benefits for children. | - Regulatory Challenges and Unregistered Facilities: Only 32% of child care institutions were registered under the JJ Act (2015), leading to a significant number of unregistered institutions. | - Need for Enhanced Monitoring and Staff Training: The welfare of children in CCIs depends heavily on effective monitoring, staff capacity building, and protection mechanisms.

PROMISE: Drastic Reduction in the cases of TB.
STATUS AND COMMENTS: - Improved case detection in 2022, recovering from pandemic losses. | - India has the highest TB burden globally, with 27% of all TB cases. | - Significant reductions in newly diagnosed TB cases in 2020 and 2021, but recovery above 2019 levels in 2022. | - India accounted for 18% of the global cases missed in 2022. | - TB incidence reduced by 16% in 2022 compared to 2015, but far from the WHO target. | - TB-related deaths decreased by 18% in 2022 compared to 2015. | - Drug-resistant TB remains a major concern. | - Challenges in adopting WHO-recommended molecular kits for TB diagnosis. | - High out-of-pocket expenditure on healthcare. | - Treatment coverage rate of 80% for estimated TB cases in 2022. | - WHO revised TB mortality figures for India in 2022.

- Inadequate healthcare infrastructure in rural areas, with a shortage of human resources. | - Noted shortfall in nurses and auxiliary nurse midwives (ANMs). | - Questionable assumptions in calculating the doctor-population ratio of 1:834, potentially not reflecting the actual availability of doctors.
